summary: Iteration 4 verifies the CRITICAL 502-on-second-turn regression from iteration_3 is fully fixed. /api/sessions/{id}/interact is now an SSE StreamingResponse (text/event-stream) with heartbeat comments during LLM generation and a terminal `event: done` carrying the full session JSON (or `event: error`). Rewrote /app/backend/tests/test_developmental_engine.py to consume the SSE stream (new sse_interact() helper). All 8 pytest tests PASS end-to-end against the public Cloudflare-fronted URL (dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com) in 98.35s total — including a full 3-turn conversation (writing → revise → answer), each turn completing well under 60s per the elapsed-time assertion baked into every turn test. Frontend end-to-end verified via Playwright on the public URL: TeacherSetup → begin-session → StudentWorkspace; three turns via writing-area/continue-button then reply-mode-revise + reply-input + send-reply-button then reply-mode-answer + send-reply-button all produce a fresh ai-invitation bubble in the conversation-thread; dev panel opens with all required labels (Current Telos, Current Organization, Observed Developmental Movement, Currently Relevant Canonical Domains, Active Tensions, Cultural Resources, Supporting + Complicating Evidence, Current Uncertainty, Candidate Invitations with candidate-invitation-0/1, Selected Invitation, Rationale, Change From Previous Interaction, Observed Reorganization) and 2 candidate-invitation-N cards; toggle-telos-editor + telos-edit-pedagogical_purpose + telos-edit-current_writing_task + save-telos-button fires a 'Telos revised' toast and the Student Workspace header immediately reflects the new current writing task; close-dev-panel-button dismisses; reloading the browser (localStorage dws_session_id) restores 3 student turns + 3 AI invitations. Regression: empty content → 400 and missing session → 404 for GET, PATCH, POST interact all confirmed. Canonical model reasoning is correct — currently_relevant_domains is a non-empty subset of the 13 canonical names on every turn (canonical names verified against /app/backend/canonical_writing_model.json), 2-3 candidate_invitations per interaction with exactly one selected_invitation presented as the student-facing invitation, and no stage/level/score/rubric language appears anywhere. Theory history preservation confirmed: theory_history grows v1 → v2 → v3, v1 preserves the empty initial theory, v2 preserves the first-turn theory's currently_relevant_domains, v3 preserves the second-turn theory's currently_relevant_domains (each snapshot captures the theory BEFORE the update, not the new theory). changes_since_previous transitions off 'initial' after turn 1.

minor.issue: Still returns 200 instead of 201 for resource creation (carried over from iteration_1/2/3, non-blocking).

issues: Carried over from prior iterations (non-blocking): the sliding dev panel (max-w-md, fixed right-0) overlays the sticky right-hand 'Conversation with your coach' column rather than being offset or pushing content. Contents remain readable when the panel is open but the right ~30% of the workspace is covered.

action_items: Optional (non-blocking): offset the dev panel or use a narrower panel width so it doesn't overlay the sticky conversation column at ~1920px.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:interact — SSE generator is correct: TextDelta chunks trigger `: tick\n\n` heartbeats that keep the connection warm past Cloudflare's ~60s edge idle-timeout, and the terminal `event: done` line carries the full session JSON parsed by both the pytest sse_interact() helper and the frontend fetch-based reader. Error path emits `event: error` with a JSON detail, also parsed by both consumers. Persistence write happens BEFORE the done event is yielded — correct ordering.

server.py:_build_prompt — the compact canonical projection (_compact_canonical_model) correctly drops the heaviest fields (differentiations/tensions/candidate_invitations/relationships) from the per-turn prompt. After turn 1, only the previously-relevant domains' compact detail plus all_domain_names is injected — small enough to keep per-turn latency comfortably under 60s (measured across all 3 turns via public URL + pytest elapsed-time assertions).

server.py:_apply_engine_result — theory_history snapshot correctly captures the PREVIOUS session.telos/session.theory BEFORE they are replaced by the new result, and version = len(history)+1. Verified end-to-end: turn 1 snapshots the empty initial theory as v1; turn 2 snapshots turn-1's theory as v2; turn 3 snapshots turn-2's theory as v3.

server.py:edit_telos — teacher_edits records a from/to diff per changed field; telos mirrors are updated consistently; telos.telos_changed is set to a human-readable marker; GET-after-PATCH returns the revised values. Verified.

api.js:interact (frontend) — SSE reader parses only `event: done` / `event: error` events, ignores `:` heartbeat comments, and rethrows a normalized Error with .detail on failure. Matches the backend format exactly.

SYSTEM_MESSAGE — the BREVITY rules (2-3 short list items per field, 2 candidate invitations preferred, terse phrase-level strings) are respected in practice: 3-turn wall-clock 98s total across the full pytest suite, no stage/score language observed in any invitation or theory blob across the run.
Carried-over from iteration_3 (still true): DevelopmentPanel.jsx TelosEditor does not expose teacher_notes even though the PATCH endpoint accepts it. Minor gap, not blocking.

rca of the issue:
Iteration_3 regression (second /interact returning 502 via public URL) is RESOLVED. Root cause was that pre-SSE the endpoint returned a single JSON body only after Claude finished (~60-80s per turn on later turns), which exceeded Cloudflare's ~60s edge idle-timeout. Fix landed in server.py: interact() is now a StreamingResponse that iterates chat.stream_message() and yields `: tick

` heartbeat comments on every TextDelta so bytes flow before the edge cap; the final `event: done
data: <session_json>

` carries the full persisted session. Prompts were also slimmed (compact canonical projection + BREVITY rules in SYSTEM_MESSAGE) so wall-clock stays comfortably under 60s. Verified end-to-end: 3-turn pytest run against the public URL — all HTTP 200 with a done event, each turn <60s (elapsed assertion in every test), theory_history preserved v1/v2/v3, no 502s across 8 tests. Playwright end-to-end verified the frontend fetch-based SSE reader consumes the stream correctly and updates conversation-thread after each turn.
